findings.reason: The protected query is concise, conventional, and interview-ready. One descriptively named ranked_students CTE assigns independent alphabetic positions, and one conditional aggregate pivots equal positions into the required America, Asia, and Europe columns without repeated continent-specific subqueries or fragile session variables. No candidate would materially improve its correctness, complexity, clarity, or structure.

ROW_NUMBER partitions rows by continent and orders each partition by name, so every table row—including a fully duplicate row—receives one rank in its alphabetic list. Grouping equal ranks aligns the kth available name from each continent. Each CASE exposes only its own continent, MAX selects that single nonnull value, an absent kth name remains null, and ORDER BY position preserves rank order.

Authenticated Premium source hash 99e26c51f543da1cbb002315f30b2f6e12a48c54f0f8e8f0b1a8e274cdaa3557, repository metadata, the Student fixture schema, and both SQL artifacts agree on varchar name and continent columns, permitted duplicate rows, alphabetical per-continent placement, America/Asia/Europe output order, and the generator guarantee that America is not smaller than Asia or Europe.

The protected app SQL and immutable MySQL source remain byte-for-byte identical and share canonical SHA-256 a2e6aad0f3cc8a58ffb36a0892785eda97ab1b9b50031069b966c13573511b27. The native artifact remains bound to verified submission 2065479475, so ranking, conditional aggregation, grouping, output ordering, schema, and data flow require no adapter-difference exception.

The unchanged 64-, 256-, and 512-row tiers span 8x, distribute reverse-ordered names across all three continents, and exercise complete ranking and pivoting. The protected source passes all ten executions at +0.02 extra growth and a maximum observed tier ratio of 1.02x. A duplicate-safe correlated predecessor-rescan control passes every output but fails only scaling at +0.81 extra growth and 10.39x on the largest tier.

The Approach now describes partitioned ROW_NUMBER ranking, duplicate-row preservation, equal-position grouping, conditional MAX pivoting, null behavior, the America-population guarantee, the generalized follow-up behavior, and the sort-dominated O(R log R) time and O(R) space bounds of the reviewed source.

The authenticated statement contains a Student schema table, description, one unexplained example with input and output tables, and a follow-up, with no constraints, images, diagrams, hints, or notes. The modular Reference preserves that order, all three table structures and data, the duplicate-row fact, the America-population guarantee, the exact example literals, the absence of an example explanation, and the source-native follow-up; source_fidelity.json validates without errors.

coverage: The sole authenticated source example appears first with the exact four Student rows in source order and exact Jack/Xi/Pascal then Jane/null/null output. It remains correctly marked as unexplained; all other fixtures are explicitly additional trials.

Every additional fixture now respects the source generator guarantee that America's population is at least Asia's and Europe's. The former Asia-only, Europe-longest, and Europe-heavier asymmetric cases were replaced with schema-valid equivalents.

A visible duplicate-row trial covers the source's explicit lack of a key by requiring two identical America rows to survive as two successive Alex values. Missing Asia and Europe, equal populations, America-longest layouts, and several asymmetric ranks cover null padding and output height.

Alphabetical ordering independent of input order, equal names, balanced and unequal populations, America/Asia/Europe column order, and preservation of every input row cover the material pivot semantics and the generalized follow-up behavior.

An independent per-continent group-sort-and-rank oracle plus SQLite execution of both byte-identical protected queries verified all seven visible cases, all three benchmark outputs, 1,355 exhaustive ordered schema-valid continent assignments through seven rows, and 1,000 deterministic randomized tables with duplicate rows and tied names using seed 61820260804.

All seven correctness cases are visible samples or trials. The unchanged 64-, 256-, and 512-row reverse-ordered workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, and a correct duplicate-safe quadratic control fails only their scaling verdict.
